partners.diseaseBName: inflammatory bowel disease, immunodeficiency, and encephalopathy
partners.mechanism_chain: TGFBR2 (HGNC:11705) —DISRUPTS→ TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-180794); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-180794) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal cellular proliferation (HP:0002161); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-180794) —LEADS_TO→ Immune dysregulation (HP:0011415); Abnormal cellular proliferation (HP:0002161) —LEADS_TO→ Inflammatory bowel disease (HP:0002727); Immune dysregulation (HP:0011415) —LEADS_TO→ Encephalopathy (HP:0001299); Immune dysregulation (HP:0011415) —LEADS_TO→ Inflammatory bowel disease (HP:0002727). Haploinsufficiency of TGFBR2 disrupts the TGF-beta signaling pathway. This disruption leads to abnormal cellular proliferation and immune dysregulation. In disease A (TGFBR2-associated disorders), abnormal cellular proliferation contributes to features like colorectal cancer, while immune dysregulation contributes to immunodeficiency. In disease B (IBD, immunodeficiency, and encephalopathy), the immune dysregulation is a direct cause of immunodeficiency and contributes to the inflammatory bowel disease, and potentially encephalopathy. The convergence occurs on the TGF-beta signaling pathway and its downstream cellular and immune consequences.

In disease A (TGFBR2-associated disorders), abnormal cellular proliferation contributes to features like colorectal cancer, while immune dysregulation contributes to immunodeficiency. In disease B (IBD, immunodeficiency, and encephalopathy), the immune dysregulation is a direct cause of immunodeficiency and contributes to the inflammatory bowel disease, and potentially encephalopathy.
